headword: {九死|きゅうし}に{一生|いっしょう}
reading: きゅうしにいっしょう

definitions.gloss: narrow escape from death; surviving against all odds
definitions.explanation: An idiom meaning to barely survive a life-threatening situation. Literally "one life out of nine deaths," expressing that the chance of survival was only one in ten.

examples.japanese: {九死|きゅうし}に{一生|いっしょう}を{得|え}た。
{交通|こうつう}{事故|じこ}で{九死|きゅうし}に{一生|いっしょう}を{得|え}て、{命|いのち}の{大切|たいせつ}さを{実感|じっかん}した。
examples.english: After narrowly surviving a traffic accident, I truly felt the preciousness of life.

examples.japanese: {登山中|とざんちゅう}に{雪崩|なだれ}に{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれたが、{九死|きゅうし}に{一生|いっしょう}を{得|え}て{救助|きゅうじょ}された。
examples.english: I was caught in an avalanche while mountain climbing, but barely survived and was rescued.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used in the set phrase {九死|きゅうし}に{一生|いっしょう}を{得|え}る (to obtain one life from nine deaths). A classical four-character idiom (yojijukugo) originating from Chinese. Used in both speech and writing to describe dramatic survival stories.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {九死|きゅうし}に{一生|いっしょう}を{得|え}る (to narrowly escape death)
- {九死|きゅうし}に{一生|いっしょう}を{得|え}た{体験|たいけん} (an experience of narrowly escaping death)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {危機一髪|ききいっぱつ}: a close call — a hair's breadth from danger; does not necessarily involve death
- {命|いのち}からがら: barely with one's life — emphasizes fleeing from danger
